summary: Union Parish fire tower near Ruston, named in a 1979 Field Day notice; a 1952-53 weather station carries its name. No source found describes it today.

events.note: Weather station named D ARBONNE FIRE DNGR TOWER has records from February 1952 to August 1953. The name suggests the tower was in use by then.
Amateur radio Field Day exercise planned at the D'Arbonne Fire Tower for the weekend after June 21, 1979; the public was invited.

corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts page spells the agency 'Forewstry', which looks like a typo for Forestry. I found no source confirming the agency's exact name, so the proposed value is unverified.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Two sources: the Forest Lookouts page (1979 Field Day notice) and an IEM weather-station page named for the tower (1952-53 archive). The IEM page reads station elevation -304 m, which is a data error. Agency correction is proposed for spelling only; 'Forestry' is unconfirmed. Wikipedia's list of Louisiana fire lookout towers, which calls itself incomplete, has no D'Arbonne entry. No built date, staffing, status or access found. anyplaceamerica.com returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Story now says the page gives the location as 20N-1W-Sec.26; the page has no 'legal location' label. The agency spelling is kept as the page prints it (see corrections, which is an unverified proposal and is not applied in the story).
